In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

c-myc is implicated in the pathogenesis and progression of Burkitt lymphoma, some cases of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and some types of small-cell carcinoma of lung, N-myc is implicated as a major determinant of the malignant phenotype in neuroblastoma, and L-myc has been shown to be involved in the pathogenesis, progression and/or maintenance of some small-cell carcinoma of the lung, and some cases of B- and T-cell acute lymphobastic leukemia.

c-myc is involved in the pathogenesis and/or progression of Burkitt's lymphoma, small-cell lung carcinoma, acute myelogenous leukemia, neuroblastoma and some other neuroectodermal tumors; N-myc is involved, as a major factor, in the pathogenesis or progression of neuroblastoma and small-cell lung carcinoma; and L-myc may be involved in the pathogeneses of some neuroectodermal and other tumors.
c-myc is associated with a wide range of human neoplastic conditions including lymphoma, leukemia, breast, colon and other carcinomas and L-myc is associated specifically with small cell lung cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MYC oncoproteins are not simply oncogenic agents, but are involved in the pathogenesis, progression and/or maintenance of a number of naturally occurring human neoplasms.
the deregulated function of each of the three MYC genes is associated with a distinct set of neoplastic diseases in humans.
MYC members play a significant role in the pathobiology of human malignancies, and the specific MYC genes involved are likely to be different in different diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MYC oncoproteins are not simply interchangeable with respect to the neoplastic diseases they cause.
, although the MYC genes are not interchangeable in terms of their functional consequences, they are not unique in their association with specific human malignancies.
MYC oncoproteins have been shown to be causally implicated in a wide array of human malignancies, and that the specific role of each member of this family is dependent upon the tissue type involved.
